statements.text: Can you discuss in this setting how Project Linchpin is integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into Army systems? [...] Will you address how this project will or will not keep a human in the loop on intelligence and targeting analyses?
statements.context: Senate Armed Services Committee hearing on the FY2024 Defense Department authorization request.

statements.text: Let's address AI. Scammers can use AI generated and power technology to do deepfakes on voice, do deepfakes on photographs. [...] We know of a New Yorker whose mother received a call from a scammer using voice cloning AI to mimic her distressed child in need of $50,000 to get her out of jail.
statements.context: Senate hearing on AI-enabled scams and consumer protection.

statements.text: Director Burns. Another example is we've seen evidence that al-Qaida in the Arabian Peninsula has used AI to generate videos aimed at inspiring lone-wolf attacks as a result to the Gaza conflict as well.
statements.context: Senator Gillibrand addresses Director Burns during the Senate Intelligence Committee's open hearing on the Worldwide Threats Assessment 2024.

statements.text: Research from the Center for Countering Digital Hate found that the leading AI image-generators create election disinformation in 41 percent of cases in which they are prompted, including images that could support false claims about candidates or election fraud, in spite of controls we've been told have been put in place.
statements.context: Senate Intelligence Committee hearing on worldwide threats, where Senator Gillibrand questions the intelligence panel about AI-enabled election disinformation.

statements.text: I gave one example, let's say an adversary decides to use AI and different kinds of generated content to spew out false information from an elected leader or a candidate to such a degree that it misleads the American public in a U.S. election.
statements.context: Senate Armed Services Committee hearing on global security challenges and US strategy, where Senator Gillibrand questions a witness about defending the homeland against cyber and AI-enabled attacks.

statements.text: We frequently hear about the growing use of AI, including generative AI in scams that target older adults. However, the same technology that helps scammers may also be used to combat these scams, as you said. [...] Can you please discuss further how AI can be used in identifying and blocking scams? Do you foresee any new opportunities for tools to combat scams based on new developments of AI?
statements.context: Senate hearing on international scams targeting seniors, where Senator Gillibrand questions a witness about AI's role in fraud prevention.

statements.text: Americans should be able to post images of themselves and their children online without fear of fake, sexualized images being produced by bullies and pedophiles.
statements.venue: Statement on letter to tech companies over AI deepfakes

statements.text: Our children should be protected from AI toys that have the potential to expose them to inappropriate concepts and compromise their privacy. The FTC has a responsibility to make sure companies protect children’s data privacy and exercise caution in making unsubstantiated claims about products intended for young children.
statements.venue: Press release on letter to FTC on AI toys

statements.text: The most critical decisions affecting our national security and the lives of our service members must always be made by human beings, not unaccountable machines. Right now, the Pentagon is moving toward deploying incredibly powerful AI technology without commonsense guardrails in place, which could have catastrophic consequences that make all of us less safe. We must act now – not to stifle technological progress, but to establish clear rules of the road that keep humans in charge and keep AI’s use in warfare smart and safe.
statements.venue: Press release on Secure and Accountable Military AI Act

statements.text: At the federal level, my mission is to ensure AI innovation benefits every American, not just a powerful few. That requires establishing clear, reliable rules of the road. We must build a framework that protects our kids from harmful algorithms and social media tools; shields seniors and consumers from AI-driven scams and fraud; and safeguards American jobs and livelihoods from displacement.
statements.venue: Press statement on NY data center moratorium

statements.text: This report serves as a roadmap for how we can protect our seniors and vulnerable populations as AI rapidly develops. By making it easier for bad actors to clone voices, fabricate images, and deceive targets, AI has facilitated an alarming rise in financial scams that rob our seniors of their hard-earned savings and personal information.
statements.venue: Senate Aging Committee press release on AI report

statements.text: The Trump administration’s unfocused, ad-hoc approach to AI risks America’s economic security and competitiveness. The American people and leading AI companies need clear rules, not constantly changing dictates from the White House. Current administration policy is a disaster, failing to address security risks while threatening American innovation and pushing the world to Chinese alternatives.
statements.venue: Press release on letter to Trump administration on frontier AI oversight

statements.text: In 2025, seniors lost nearly $8 billion to scams. That’s up over 50% from the year before, due in part to the increasing sophistication of AI technology. Scammers use AI to generate deepfake images, clone voices, and launch phishing attacks that drain seniors’ savings. In many cases, AI didn’t invent these scams—it supercharged them, making old cons more convincing and easier to pull off.
statements.venue: Weekly media remarks on AI scams, as published by Staten Islander

statements.text: We need urgent engagement now. We need to be able to have rules of the road, we need to be able to have reliable guardrails, and we need to be able to be talking to these AI companies regularly about how to do this well, how to maintain our leadership, how to maintain the ability to cure cancer and cure disease, and have massive breakthroughs.
statements.venue: CNN Situation Room interview (transcript on Senate website)

statements.text: And I do not think President Trump is providing any leadership on this. He’s sold the most efficient chips to China, but again, not making sure that we have rules of the road that our own AI companies can ensure that the public is safe.
statements.venue: CNN Situation Room interview (transcript on Senate website)

statements.text: These AI models must be aligned with humanity. Humanity has to be the focus. I worked in our defense bill over the last several months to try to put a human in the loop on all systems and to make sure AI couldn’t be used for domestic surveillance.
statements.venue: CNN Situation Room interview (transcript on Senate website)
